/usr/lib/apt/methods/http.why: Browsers can't open TCP connections: tabcomputer's transport fetches from the page's same-origin mirror. apt still verifies the signed InRelease and every hash.

/usr/lib/apt/methods/store.why: apt decompresses every downloaded index through this method; under the x86 engine xz-decoding trixie's 56 MB Packages took ~33 s of `apt-get update`. tabcomputer's runs the same codecs and hashes natively; apt still checks the result against the signed Release file.

/usr/sbin/dpkg-preconfigure.why: apt-utils' 70debconf hook runs this before every dpkg run; under DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive it has nothing to ask but cost ~20 s per install under the x86 engine (Perl, debconf, apt-extracttemplates). tabcomputer's drains apt's list and exits 0 then (templates load at configure time through the confmodule, as without apt-utils) and runs Debian's script, kept as dpkg-preconfigure.debian, for any other frontend.

/usr/bin/apt-get.why: apt keeps working after an install stopped part-way (a closed tab, a transient engine fault): before a command that changes packages tabcomputer's runs `dpkg --configure -a` when dpkg was interrupted and `apt-get -f install` when packages were left half-installed, and an install that fails part-way is recovered and retried once (its downloaded archives are reused). Everything else, and the commands themselves, are Debian's apt, kept as apt-get.debian.
